Stoneham Park Academy
Welcome toStoneham ParkPrimary Academy
Thank you for your interest in our school. Stoneham Park Academy is a brand new 315 place primary academy for children aged 4-11. We are very proud to be sponsored by the University of Winchester.
Newly opened in September 2020 to Year R pupils and situated at the heart of the new North Stoneham development in Eastleigh, our school offers a high quality, values driven education.
Aspirational Inspiring Inclusive Sustainable Joyful
Please get in touch with us if you would like to know more about our wonderful new school or if you would like to come along to one of our open events.

Welcome to Stoneham Park
Have a wonderful summer - we will see you back at school on Wednesday 2nd September!
Are you looking for a place for your child at Stoneham Park?
We have limited spaces in our September Y3, Y4, Y5 & Y6 classes - applications can be made now via Hampshire Admissions. If you would like to visit the school for a place in these year groups then please email: admin@stonehampark.uwinat.co.uk
Our September YR, Y1 & Y2 classes are all full with waiting lists. Please do apply on Hampshire Admissions if you are looking for a place in these classes and you will be added to the waiting list. We can then offer you a tour if a place becomes available.

Stoneham Park Academy
Prospective parent information and school visits
Thank you for your interest in Stoneham Park Primary Academy.
Please use the appropriate drop down menu here:
My child is starting school in september 2026
If your child is 4 or will turn 4 before 1st September 2026, they can start school in September 2026. For more information go to www.hants.gov.uk/admissions
Starting School Flyer 2026.pdf
We are holding a number of open events with Mrs Fahey for parents/carers of Year R admissions for a September 2026 start. These events involve a tour of the school and a presentation with lots of useful information about our wonderful school.
Tuesday 16th September 2025
Thursday 2nd October 2025
Tuesday 7th October 2025
Monday 20th October 2025
Tuesday 4th November 2025
Tuesday 18th November 2025
Thursday 11th December 2025
Our open events are now complete for this year and the application deadline has passed.
How to book an appointment?
Please email the school office on admin@stonehampark.uwinat.co.uk to book your slot to visit on any of the available dates above. It would be helpful in your email if you can please include:
Hampshire Admissions - Starting school in Hampshire booklet
If you have made your decision, in order to make your application for your child's place starting in Year R in September 2026, please click here to visit Hampshire Admissions
your name
a contact telephone number
an email address
I would like to transfer my child to stoneham park primary academy from another school
If you are looking to move your child to us from another school, then please be advised that we have a limited number of spaces in Year 2, Year 3, Year 4 and Year 5 for an immediate start (as at April 2026) and we have waiting lists for Year R & Year 3. As a new school, we grow by one year group each year and currently do not yet have a Year 6 cohort.
Please contact the school office (admin@stonehampark.uwinat.co.uk) for the most up to date details of places available and also make an In-Year Application via Hampshire Admissions.
My child is starting school in september 2027
If your child is 4 or will turn 4 before 1st September 2027, they can start school in September 2027. For more information go to www.hants.gov.uk/admissions
Applications open for Hampshire residents on 1st November 2026 and close 15th January 2027 - any applications after the closing date will be processed as a late application.
We will hold a number of open events with Mrs Fahey for parents/carers of Year R admissions for a September 2027 start. These events involve a tour of the school and a presentation with lots of useful information about our wonderful school.
We will not release dates for school tours until September 2026. All details will appear here when available

Attendance & Absence
At Stoneham Park Primary Academy, all pupils are expected to arrive on time for school every day of the school year.
Absence reporting
If your child is unable to attend school, please contact the school office to report their absence via telephone on 02380 518833. Ideally this should be prior to 9am please.
We will need your child's name, class and the reason for absence.
As a safety measure, we will need to telephone and/or email all contacts if a child is not at school and their absence hasn't been reported.
If your child has an unavoidable medical appointment during the school day then please forward the medical appointment letter on email to admin@stonehampark.uwinat.co.uk
Whilst we understand that some appointments will need to take place in the school day, we do expect appointments to be out of school hours or in school holidays where possible.
sickness
The links below to the NHS provide valuable information about common illnesses in children and how long the NHS recommend children to stay off school.
One of the most common reminders that we have to make to parents/carers is the 48 hour rule after sickness or diarrhoea. Your child must remain off school 48 hours after the last episode. Please do use these links as a point of reference:
Can my child go to school today?
Is my child too ill for school? (NHS)
When your child is well enough to return to school after illness, we can administer medicines prescribed by your GP, with the pharmacy label in tact and if the medicine is to be taken four times per day. Please see our medicine policies below for further information:
Supporting pupils with medical conditions
Administration of Medicines Policy
Administration of Medicines Treatment Consent Form (for prescribed medicines that are to be taken 4 times a day)
Absence request forms
For any period of planned absence, you will need to print off the form below, fill it in and return it to the school office. Alternatively, the school office hold copies if you do not have access to a printer.
As per our Attendance policy (which can be found in full at the bottom of this page):
Request for Leave of Absence:
Amendments to school attendance regulations were updated and enforced from September 2013: (Pupil registration) (England) regulations state that Headteachers may not grant any leave of absence during term time unless there are exceptional circumstances. It is important to note that Headteachers can determine the length of the authorised absence as well as whether absence is authorised at all. The fundamental principles for defining ‘exceptional’ are rare, significant, or unavoidable which means the event could not reasonably be scheduled at another time. There are no rules on this as circumstances vary from school to school and family to family. There is however, no legal entitlement for time off in school time to go on holiday and in the majority of cases holiday will not be authorised. Parents/Carers wishing to apply for leave of absence need to fill in an application form (available from the school office) in advance and before making any travel arrangements.
If term time leave is taken without prior permission from the school, the absence will be unauthorised and if the number of sessions absent hits the thresholds set down in Hampshire’s Code of Conduct parent/carers will be issued with a fixed-penalty fine, or other legal action in accordance the code (see section 6 for detail).
Taking holidays in term time will affect your child’s schooling as much as any other absence and we expect parents to help us by not taking children out during school time.

Guitar, drums & Keyboard Lessons - during the school day (Wednesday mornings)
The Winchester Academy of Modern Music (WAMM) are continuing to provide music lessons at Stoneham offering the following for 2026-27:
All payments and arrangements will be made directly through WAMM.
For prices please contact WAMM direct. The price includes access to WAMM’s fantastic online portal, all necessary music books and resources, exciting performance opportunities throughout the year, and two detailed written reports (sent home in December and July) outlining your child’s progress. Students will receive a guaranteed minimum of 36 lessons across the academic year.
Led by passionate musician Ben Goddard, WAMM supports and inspires over 200 young musicians every week. Ben and his team of professional, performing musicians are committed to delivering lessons that are fun, motivating, and full of real-world expertise. Ben says:

PSHE Association Curriculum Overview
PSHE Curriculum Overview
The PSHE Association describes Personal, Social and Health Education as givingpupils the knowledge, skills and attributes they need to keep themselves healthand safe, preparing them for life and work in modern Britain. It teaches pupilsabout transferable skills including self awareness, empathy, communication andteamwork, supports pupils in their wellbeing and helps them to manage issueswhich could affect their ability to learn, such as anxiety and unhappyrelationships.Stoneham Park Primary Acdemy, PSHE is delivered through three levels:
By the end of their time in Key Stage 2, our aim is that children will be able todemonstrate that they recognise their own worth and that of others, to expresstheir views confidently and listen to and show respect for the views of others.
They will be able to identify positive ways to face new challenges, discusschanges they will go through and demonstrate some ways of dealing with thesein a positive way. They will explain how they will develop skills to work in thefuture and make choices about how to develop healthy lifestyles for body andmind.
They will make judgements and decisions, list ways of resisting negativepeer pressure and explain how to manage risks in different familiar situations.Children will be able to explain how their actions have consequences forthemselves and others. They will be able to describe the nature andconsequences of bullying, and express ways of responding to it. They will be able to respond to negative behaviours such as stereotyping and aggression and demonstrate respect and tolerance towards people different from themselves.
Each year group from 1-6 has the same focus topic each half term using the 'Thought Box' scheme of work. Objectives, resources and activities are differentiated within each topic. Approaches to teaching approaches vary and include (but are not limited to): Debates, Group/Individual Research & presentation, Draw & Write, Drama & Role Play, Group/Individual Writing tasks and Circle Times. In addition, other ongoing class practices and collective worship themes can also address and teach the objectives.
As part of our 'Dream Catcher' visitor programme we invite in professionals and members of the community to add to the provision and provide expertknowledge and memorable experiences. For example, air ambulance crew visits, Winchester Basics Bank staff and the NSPCC.
The benefits for pupils from PSHE education are relevant both now and in thefuture and link very clearly to our Trust values. Knowledge and skills such as being able to sustain healthy & safe relationships, establishing a good sense of self awareness, together with an ability to manage risk, experience change and communicate effectively are helpful for pupils being able to thrive as individuals, family members and members of society. It will help children to manage many significant opportunities and challenges they will face growing up. Some of these are detailed in this linked document produced by the PSHE association.
Our PSHE curriculum for Early Years is delivered through the 7 aspects of the EYFS framework as well as participation in whole school events.
